item.title: Agents Need Version Control Too
item.description: Every serious AI coding deployment eventually collides with the same wall: the agent's work has no history. Prompts, tool calls, and generated diffs live in a chat log, not a repository. The fix is boring and structural. Treat every agent run as a branch: commit the environment, commit the output, review the diff, merge or discard. Teams that adopt this ship agents to production, and teams that skip it keep pasting context back into a fresh chat every morning. Git was built for exactly this discipline. The workflow guide for agent version control is on pastagi dot com.

item.title: What a Support Agent Actually Saves
item.description: Vendors pitch AI support agents as headcount replacement. The real savings math is narrower and still compelling. An agent deflects the top forty percent of ticket volume: password resets, order status, refund policy. Those tickets cost a few dollars each to answer and the agent answers them for cents. The remaining sixty percent, escalations and edge cases, still routes to humans, and the agent's real value there is a summarized transcript that cuts handle time by a third. Model the stack that way and the payback window is months, not years. The decoded vendor table is on pastagi dot com.
